title: Encrypt device tools end to end and enable consented native desktop control.
changes: Add authenticated RFC 9180 HPKE for paired-device tool requests, results, errors and native WebRTC SDP, with independent fingerprint pins, pairing-bound OS-vault identities, explicit read/control peer grants, replay protection and bounded encrypted chunks.

Add local AI stdio access with remcp e2ee client-init, client-pin, client-login and remcp mcp --device; negotiate the dedicated opaque MCP transport without exposing a generic executor to ordinary or review clients.

Add per-account/device nonexportable browser keys, independent device pinning, enrollment controls and encrypted native desktop control in the workspace. State browser JavaScript delivery trust and authorized endpoint visibility explicitly.

Install optional source-only native media with remcp desktop install --python , using an owner-private environment and pinned vendor wheel hashes. Support Windows interactive desktop, macOS Screen Recording and Linux Wayland/PipeWire consent without additional native binary bundles.

Bind remote input to the explicitly approved active media session and increasing sequence numbers. Confirm native process exit and drain queued input before acknowledging Stop; reject input after Stop and preserve clipboard text exactly within its bounded transfer limit.

Fetch short-lived, destination-pinned TURN configuration as the paired agent and deliver it only through private local runtime stdio. Keep caller metadata and relay-provided tool arguments from injecting native ICE configuration.
Stop the runtime on permanent pairing/account revocation; preserve temporary disabled-device recovery and fail-closed strict encryption policy across service reloads.

Activate the independent production MCP resource at mcp.remcp.site with dedicated PostgreSQL/Redis credentials, TLS, issuer-bound RS256 verification and resource-scoped OAuth. Preserve the canonical remcp.site issuer and legacy MCP endpoint.

Preserve 10 compact hosted definitions and 178 individually reviewed operations; add two capability-checked native media operations to the 93-operation runtime. Keep DLL-free Windows source integrity, immutable public release parity and trusted package publishing.
